title: Incremental model comparator and exposure governor for safe rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a reusable A/B comparison controller and exposure governor that operators can bind to any model route to run gradual comparisons (canary and A/B) with automatic stop/rollback triggers. This ticket scopes the experiment controller behaviors, exposure throttles, statistical test suite, UX hooks for the Console, and integration points for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Why: Current rollouts rely on ad-hoc scripts and manual monitoring. We need a declarative, policy-driven controller that reduces human error, enforces exposure caps, and provides fast automated rollback when safety or quality guards trip.

Non-goals: Full cohort cohorting engine (advanced cohorting will be separate), metric ingestion pipeline changes (we consume existing metric feeds), or replacing existing canary runner UX — this integrates into the Console and runtime routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A controller API that accepts: baseline model id, candidate model id(s), exposure schedule, guard policies, and stop conditions. 2) Console UI shows live exposure, metric deltas, and the active policy. 3) The controller automatically reduces or stops exposure per configured guard triggers and emits audit log events. 4) Integration test coverage demonstrating a synthetic regression triggers auto-rollback in a dedicated environment. 5) Documentation and runbook added to Confluence and Console help.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (pre-prod): run synthetic experiments in 'canary-preprod' with 0.1% synthetic traffic to verify metric signal and audit events. Stage 2 (internal): enable 'internal' cohort (10% exposure) for 48 hours with manual approvals. Stage 3 (gradual public): ramp to 1% -> 5% -> 20% using a 3-step schedule with automated checks at each step. Final: either promote candidate to ’primary’ or fully rollback and create a postmortem. All steps require route pinning and capacity reservations for Dedicated customers.
statistical_checks: Primary metrics: latency p95, token-cost-per-response, and business metric (e.g., answer-accuracy proxy or rerank-NDCG). Secondary: error-rate, hallucination-rate heuristics, and variance of generation length. Testing approach: sequential hypothesis testing with pre-defined alpha/beta: use a two-sided sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) for latency and a Bayesian credible interval for quality metrics. Stopping rules: reject candidate if p-value < 0.01 for regression on critical metric OR posterior probability that candidate is worse by >= X% > 0.95. Minimum sample size guard: do not consider decision until N_min (default 2000 requests per metric) observed. Statistical telemetry stored in ExperimentEvents table and surfaced in Console.
exposure_controls:
Policies supported: fixed-percent, scheduled-ramp, cohort-weighted (internal/beta/public), and shadow-only (no user-visible effects). Safety knobs: global max_exposure (default 25%), per-customer max_exposure override, per-route blacklists, and emergency_quarantine that sets exposure to 0 instantly. Rate limiting: controller respects runtime throughput caps and credits to avoid overloading backend GPUs. Exposure config example (YAML):

exposure:
  mode: scheduled-ramp
  steps:
    - percent: 1
      duration_hours: 4
    - percent: 5
      duration_hours: 12
    - percent: 20
      duration_hours: 24
  guards:
    - metric: latency_p95
      comparator: greater_than
      threshold: 1.2
      window: 10m
      action: rollback

This YAML will be supported by the Console and API.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: per-experiment time series (exposure, control vs candidate metrics, sample counts), drift indicators, and a heatmap of route impact. Alerts: Severity-1 (auto-rollback triggered), Severity-2 (metric delta > warning threshold), Severity-3 (slow steady drift). Alert destinations: PagerDuty for SRE, Slack experiment channel for PM/Eng, and email to customer success for impacted accounts. Audit logs: every exposure change and policy action must be recorded with user, timestamp, and rationale.
operational_runbook: Immediate actions on auto-rollback: 1) Controller posts incident to #experiments-incidents with links to experiment ID and most recent diffs. 2) Runbook steps: collect top 5 failing requests (redacted), compare tokens/cost, snapshot environment metrics, and if high customer impact open a Sev with CS & SRE. Postmortem template required before re-attempt. Manual override buttons on Console to pause/resume experiments.
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller state machine, integration test that replays recorded traffic into a two-model setup (baseline/candidate) and verifies triggers, load test to ensure controller scales to 200k concurrent experiments (synthetic). Canary pre-prod run scheduled 2025-02-20 (automated).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy metrics lead to false positives -> Mitigation: require sustained signal over window and minimum sample size; use hierarchical checks across multiple metrics. Risk: heavy experiments overload inference clusters -> Mitigation: controller enforces credits and integrated autoscaling policies; dry-run mode applies routing without execution. Risk: privacy/regulatory concerns for customer cohorts -> Mitigation: add per-customer opt-out and audit logs; sensitive customers default to zero exposure.
open_questions: Should the controller expose a DSL for complex guard predicates (AND/OR across metrics) or only a simple rule list?
How do we surface Bayesian vs frequentist decision rationale in Console to non-statisticians?
Do Dedicated customers get a guaranteed soft-cap that pauses experiments when capacity is low?
next_steps: 1) ENG: implement controller alpha with APIs and audit log events (ENG-5012). 2) DX: Console wireframes and API UX review (PM -> design review session 2025-02-25). 3) SRE: run load tests and add PagerDuty escalation. 4) Legal/Security: complete security review by 2025-03-05. 5) Schedule pre-prod canary and run the synthetic regression test.
